note: Taiwan says 計程車 (or casually 小黃, since taxis are yellow); 出租車 and 打的 sound mainland. You 搭/坐 a taxi, or 叫車 by phone or app.

example.zh: 我們搭計程車去夜市吧。
example.en: Let's take a taxi to the night market.

note: Nickname from the yellow paint all Taiwanese taxis use. Note the Taiwan classifier 台 for vehicles: 一台小黃.

example.zh: 下雨了，叫一台小黃比較快。
example.en: It's raining, calling a cab will be quicker.

note: Every metro system in Taiwan (Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Kaohsiung) is a 捷運. 地鐵 is understood but sounds mainland. Lines have names like 板南線 and 淡水信義線.

example.zh: 搭捷運到台北車站只要十分鐘。
example.en: It's only ten minutes to Taipei Main Station by MRT.

note: Mainland 公交(車); Taiwan 公車. Bus stop = 公車站. Raise your hand to stop the bus and tap your card when you board (and often when you get off too).

example.zh: 這班公車有到師大嗎？
example.en: Does this bus go to NTNU?

note: Same word as mainland 高铁, but in Taiwan it means the one west-coast line (南港 to 左營). 坐高鐵 / 搭高鐵.

example.zh: 坐高鐵去高雄不到兩個小時。
example.en: It takes under two hours to Kaohsiung by high-speed rail.

note: The regular railway. Train classes: 區間車 (local, stops everywhere, no reserved seats), 自強號 (express). East-coast tickets sell out on holidays.

example.zh: 坐台鐵去花蓮，沿路風景很漂亮。
example.en: Taking the train to Hualien, the scenery along the way is beautiful.

note: The standard transit card; also pays at convenience stores. The other main card is 一卡通 (iPASS). Mainland equivalent: a city 交通卡.

example.zh: 我的悠遊卡快沒錢了，要先去加值。
example.en: My EasyCard is almost empty, I need to top it up first.

note: Used for 悠遊卡 and other cards at MRT machines or convenience stores. For apps and accounts people also say 儲值. 充值 is understood but not the Taiwan word.

example.zh: 麻煩幫我悠遊卡加值五百。
example.en: Please top up my EasyCard with 500.

note: In Taiwan almost always a scooter, the main way people get around. 騎機車 = ride a scooter. On the mainland 机车 means a locomotive. Also slang for 'annoying' (see the separate entry).

example.zh: 我每天騎機車上班。
example.en: I ride my scooter to work every day.

note: Also 單車, and 自行車 in formal writing. The shared-bike system is YouBike (微笑單車).

example.zh: 週末要不要去河濱騎腳踏車？
example.en: Want to go cycling along the riverside this weekend?

note: The painted boxes along the street; 機車停車格 for scooters. 停車位 is also used, but 停車格 is very Taiwan.

example.zh: 這附近都找不到停車格。
example.en: I can't find a parking space anywhere around here.

note: Same word as the mainland. Attendants usually fill up for you: say 九五無鉛，加滿 ('95 unleaded, fill it up').

example.zh: 我先去加油站加個油。
example.en: I'll stop at the gas station to fill up first.

note: Required on scooters. Mainland says 头盔; in Taiwan 頭盔 sounds like armour or sports gear.

example.zh: 騎機車一定要戴安全帽。
example.en: You must wear a helmet on a scooter.

note: Mainland 堵车; Taiwan 塞車, also 很塞 'really jammed'.

example.zh: 下班時間國道一定塞車。
example.en: The freeway is always jammed at rush hour.

note: 禁止迴轉 = no U-turns. 迴轉壽司 = conveyor-belt sushi.

example.zh: 前面路口可以迴轉嗎？
example.en: Can I make a U-turn at the next intersection?

note: Mainland 站台; Taiwan 月台, as in 第二月台.

example.zh: 往南港的列車在第二月台。
example.en: Trains to Nangang leave from platform 2.

note: 國光客運, 統聯客運 and others; cheaper than trains. 轉運站 = bus terminal. Chartered tour buses are 遊覽車.

example.zh: 我搭客運回台中，比高鐵便宜很多。
example.en: I take the coach back to Taichung, it's much cheaper than the HSR.

note: MRT signs say 轉乘; tapping the same card gives 轉乘優惠 (transfer discounts) between bus and MRT.

example.zh: 在台北車站轉乘板南線。
example.en: Transfer to the Bannan line at Taipei Main Station.

note: Colloquially 運將 (from Japanese via Hokkien). People address a driver as 司機大哥.

example.zh: 計程車司機很熟這邊的路。
example.en: The taxi driver knows the roads around here well.

note: The covered sidewalk under the second floor of street-front buildings, typical of Taiwanese streets and often full of parked scooters.

example.zh: 下雨的時候走騎樓就不會淋濕。
example.en: When it rains you can walk under the arcades and stay dry.

note: Addresses go 路/街 (road) → 巷 (lane) → 弄 (alley off a lane), e.g. 100巷5弄3號. 弄 in addresses is read lòng.

example.zh: 這家咖啡廳藏在巷弄裡，很難找。
example.en: This café is hidden in the alleys, it's hard to find.

note: Taiwan uses 體 where the mainland uses 件: 軟體 / 硬體. An app is 應用程式 or just App.

example.zh: 這個軟體要先更新才能用。
example.en: You have to update this software before you can use it.

note: Pairs with 軟體. 硬體設備 = hardware/equipment; also used for physical facilities.

example.zh: 電腦的硬體還不錯，只是軟體太舊。
example.en: The computer's hardware is decent, it's just the software that's too old.

note: Taiwan 網路 (路 'road'); mainland 网络. 上網 = go online; 網路很慢 = the internet is slow.

example.zh: 這裡的網路好慢喔。
example.en: The internet here is so slow.

note: Any video is 影片 in Taiwan; 視頻 sounds mainland. Classifier is often 支 or 部. 拍影片 = film a video.

example.zh: 他拍了一支影片放上YouTube。
example.en: He filmed a video and put it on YouTube.

note: Taiwan 視訊 = video call or webcam. 視訊會議 = video conference.

example.zh: 晚上我要跟家人視訊。
example.en: I'm video-calling my family tonight.

note: Taiwan 資訊 where the mainland says 信息: 資訊工程 = computer science, 資訊業 = IT industry.

example.zh: 我大學念資訊工程。
example.en: I studied computer science in college.

note: The everyday word for a LINE or chat message: 傳訊息 = send a message. 息 is read xí in Taiwan.

example.zh: 我剛剛傳訊息給你，你有看到嗎？
example.en: I just sent you a message, did you see it?

note: For actual SMS (verification codes, bank alerts). Chat-app messages are 訊息.

example.zh: 驗證碼會用簡訊傳給你。
example.en: The verification code will be sent to you by text.

note: Taiwan uses 碟 (dié) where the mainland uses 盘: 硬碟, 光碟 (CD/DVD), 隨身碟. 外接硬碟 = external drive.

example.zh: 我的外接硬碟快滿了。
example.en: My external hard drive is almost full.

note: Literally 'carry-with-you disk'. Nobody in Taiwan says U盤.

example.zh: 資料存在隨身碟裡給我就好。
example.en: Just give me the files on a flash drive.

note: 'Sliding mouse'. 無線滑鼠 = wireless mouse.

example.zh: 我的滑鼠沒電了。
example.en: My mouse is out of battery.

note: Phone, computer and TV screens are all 螢幕. 截圖 = screenshot.

example.zh: 手機螢幕摔破了。
example.en: I dropped my phone and cracked the screen.

note: Short for 筆記型電腦. On the mainland 笔记本 can mean a laptop; in Taiwan 筆記本 is only a paper notebook.

example.zh: 我帶筆電去咖啡廳工作。
example.en: I take my laptop to work at a café.

note: Taiwan 列印; mainland 打印. A printer is 印表機. 影印 = photocopy.

example.zh: 幫我把這份資料列印兩份。
example.en: Please print two copies of this.

note: Convenience stores have 影印機. 影本 = a photocopy (e.g. 身分證影本).

example.zh: 申請的時候要附上身分證影本。
example.en: You need to attach a copy of your ID card with the application.

note: 寫程式 = to code; 程式設計 = programming; 應用程式 = app. Mainland 程序.

example.zh: 他每天都在寫程式。
example.en: He writes code every day.

note: Taiwan uses 資料 for both 'materials' and 'data' (資料庫 database, 資料分析 data analysis); 數據 exists but is narrower (numerical figures).

example.zh: 這些資料一定要備份。
example.en: This data definitely needs to be backed up.

note: 數位相機 digital camera, 數位化 digitize. Mainland uses 数字 / 数码.

example.zh: 很多老照片都已經數位化了。
example.en: Lots of old photos have already been digitized.

note: 檔 is read dǎng in Taiwan. 存檔 = save; 開檔 = open a file. On the mainland 档案 means archives or a dossier, and a file is 文件.

example.zh: 記得先存檔再關掉。
example.en: Remember to save the file before closing it.

note: 登出 = log out; 帳號 = account; 密碼 = password.

example.zh: 請先登入你的帳號。
example.en: Please log in to your account first.

note: The phone's Settings app is 設定. 預設 = default. Also general 'to set' (設定目標).

example.zh: 去設定裡面把通知關掉。
example.en: Go into settings and turn off notifications.

note: 貼連結 = paste a link; 點連結 = click a link.

example.zh: 我把連結貼在群組裡了。
example.en: I pasted the link in the group chat.

note: Google is a 搜尋引擎. In speech people also say 上網查 or google 一下.

example.zh: 你自己上網搜尋一下就有了。
example.en: Just search online yourself and you'll find it.

note: A transliteration of 'blog'. 部落客 = blogger.

example.zh: 她的旅遊部落格很多人看。
example.en: Lots of people read her travel blog.

note: Taiwan's key industry: 晶片, 半導體 (semiconductors), 晶圓 (wafers). TSMC is 台積電.

example.zh: 台灣的晶片產業很重要。
example.en: Taiwan's chip industry is very important.

note: Taiwan uses 智慧 where the mainland uses 智能: 智慧手錶, 人工智慧.

example.zh: 現在連阿嬤都有智慧型手機。
example.en: Now even grandma has a smartphone.

note: Usually just 'AI' in speech. Same 智慧/智能 contrast.

example.zh: 很多公司都在研究人工智慧。
example.en: Lots of companies are researching AI.

note: Taiwan uses 行動 for 'mobile': 行動電話, 行動支付, 行動網路.

example.zh: 你有帶行動電源嗎？我手機快沒電了。
example.en: Did you bring a power bank? My phone's almost dead.

note: LINE Pay, 街口, Apple Pay. Cash is still very common in Taiwan, especially at night markets.

example.zh: 這家店可以用行動支付嗎？
example.en: Can I pay with my phone at this shop?

note: 伺服器掛了 = the server is down.

example.zh: 網站的伺服器掛了。
example.en: The website's server is down.

note: A post on Facebook, Instagram or Threads. 發文 = to post.

example.zh: 她的貼文一下就有幾千個讚。
example.en: Her post got thousands of likes right away.

note: 讚 = a like; 按讚 'press like'. Mainland 点赞.

example.zh: 記得幫我們的粉專按讚。
example.en: Remember to like our fan page.

note: 有興趣請私訊 (DM if interested) is common on sale posts.

example.zh: 有興趣的話可以私訊我。
example.en: DM me if you're interested.

en: to support (a format or feature); backup help
note: 這支手機不支援… = this phone doesn't support…. Also 'reinforcements': 派人去支援. 支持 in Taiwan means support in the sense of backing a person or idea.

example.zh: 這台電腦不支援這個格式。
example.en: This computer doesn't support this format.

note: Taiwan 訊號; reception is 收訊 (這裡收訊不好).

example.zh: 山上手機沒什麼訊號。
example.en: There's hardly any phone signal up in the mountains.

note: Taiwan transliterates with 駭 'alarming'. The Matrix is 駭客任務 in Taiwan.

example.zh: 公司的網站被駭客入侵了。
example.en: The company website was hacked.

note: Taiwan only says 鳳梨 (Hokkien ông-lâi sounds like 'prosperity comes', so it's lucky). 鳳梨酥 = pineapple cake.

example.zh: 這盒鳳梨酥是要送朋友的。
example.en: This box of pineapple cakes is a gift for a friend.

note: Never call a potato 土豆 in Taiwan: 土豆 means peanuts here (from Hokkien thôo-tāu). Mashed potato = 馬鈴薯泥.

example.zh: 咖哩裡面要加馬鈴薯跟紅蘿蔔。
example.en: Curry needs potatoes and carrots in it.

note: The everyday Taiwan word (mainland 卷心菜 / 圆白菜 / 包菜). 高麗菜水餃 is a classic dumpling filling.

example.zh: 炒一盤高麗菜好了。
example.en: Let's just get a plate of stir-fried cabbage.

note: Taiwan says 番茄, never 西紅柿. Ketchup = 番茄醬; cherry tomatoes = 小番茄.

example.zh: 我很喜歡吃小番茄。
example.en: I really like cherry tomatoes.

note: Baked sweet potatoes (烤地瓜) are sold at 7-Eleven. 地瓜球 = fried sweet-potato balls at night markets.

example.zh: 超商的烤地瓜很好吃。
example.en: The baked sweet potatoes at convenience stores are really good.

note: A transliteration of 'kiwi'.

example.zh: 奇異果的維他命C很多。
example.en: Kiwis have lots of vitamin C.

note: From Hokkien pa-la̍h. Slang: 芭樂歌 = cheesy mainstream pop song; 芭樂票 = a promise that won't be kept.

example.zh: 夏天的芭樂又脆又甜。
example.en: Summer guavas are crunchy and sweet.

note: 酪 is read luò in Taiwan. 酪梨牛奶 (avocado milk) is a Taiwanese drink.

example.zh: 我早餐吃酪梨吐司。
example.en: I had avocado toast for breakfast.

note: Local oranges are 柳丁; orange juice is 柳橙汁. 橘子 = tangerine.

example.zh: 這杯柳橙汁是現榨的。
example.en: This orange juice is freshly squeezed.

note: 綠花椰(菜) = broccoli, 白花椰(菜) = cauliflower. Mainland 西兰花 / 菜花.

example.zh: 便當的配菜有綠花椰。
example.en: The bento side dishes include broccoli.

note: 洋芋 is the Taiwan snack-word for potato (樂事 Lay's).

example.zh: 看電影一定要配洋芋片。
example.en: Movies have to come with potato chips.

note: Literally 'soaked noodles'. 泡一碗泡麵 = make a bowl of instant noodles.

example.zh: 半夜肚子餓就泡一碗泡麵。
example.en: When I'm hungry at midnight I make a bowl of instant noodles.

note: From 'yogurt'. The drinkable kind is 優酪乳 (yōu luò rǔ). 酸奶 is understood but not used.

example.zh: 我早餐吃優格加水果。
example.en: I have yogurt with fruit for breakfast.

note: On drink-shop menus 鮮奶茶 / 紅茶拿鐵 use real milk, while plain 奶茶 often uses creamer (奶精).

example.zh: 我要一杯紅茶拿鐵，要鮮奶的。
example.en: I'd like a black-tea latte, made with fresh milk.

note: A transliteration of 'cheese'; 乳酪 (rǔ luò) is the more formal word.

example.zh: 我要一份起司蛋餅。
example.en: I'll have a cheese egg crepe.

note: 鮪魚飯糰 tuna rice ball, 鮪魚三明治. Salmon is 鮭魚 in Taiwan (mainland 三文鱼).

example.zh: 我要一個鮪魚飯糰。
example.en: I'll have a tuna rice ball.

note: Taiwan transliteration.

example.zh: 今天晚上叫披薩來吃吧。
example.en: Let's order pizza tonight.

note: Taiwan writes Italy as 義大利.

example.zh: 這家的青醬義大利麵很好吃。
example.en: This place's pesto pasta is great.

note: From Japanese bentō. Everywhere at lunch: 排骨便當, 雞腿便當, 台鐵便當. 便當店 = bento shop.

example.zh: 中午訂便當，你要吃什麼？
example.en: We're ordering bento for lunch, what do you want?

note: Same characters as the mainland word, reversed. 吃宵夜 is a much-loved Taiwanese habit.

example.zh: 我們去吃宵夜好不好？
example.en: Shall we go get a late-night snack?

note: Very trendy in Taiwanese cities; 早午餐店 are everywhere.

example.zh: 週末一起去吃早午餐吧。
example.en: Let's go for brunch this weekend.

note: Taiwanese-Western breakfast shops sell 蛋餅, 吐司, 漢堡 and 奶茶. The owner will probably call you 帥哥 or 美女.

example.zh: 巷口的早餐店蛋餅很好吃。
example.en: The breakfast shop at the end of the lane makes great egg crepes.

note: A thin pancake rolled with egg; add 起司, 鮪魚, 玉米 or 培根.

example.zh: 我要一份玉米蛋餅跟一杯大冰奶。
example.en: I'll have a corn egg crepe and a large iced milk tea.

note: Traditional 飯糰 is sticky rice wrapped around 油條, pork floss and pickled radish; convenience-store triangle onigiri are also called 飯糰.

example.zh: 傳統飯糰要加蛋嗎？
example.en: Do you want egg in your traditional rice roll?

note: Rice topped with minced braised pork; national comfort food. In southern Taiwan 肉燥飯 is the more common name.

example.zh: 一碗滷肉飯，再加一顆滷蛋。
example.en: A bowl of braised pork rice, plus a braised egg.

note: 紅燒 (braised, rich broth) vs 清燉 (clear broth).

example.zh: 這家的紅燒牛肉麵很有名。
example.en: This place's braised beef noodle soup is famous.

en: Taiwanese fried chicken bites (and the snack stand)
note: Also written 鹽酥雞. The stand fries whatever you pick (雞肉, 甜不辣, 四季豆) and seasons it with pepper salt and basil. They'll ask 要辣嗎？

example.zh: 鹹酥雞要不要加辣？
example.en: Do you want your fried chicken spicy?

note: Giant night-market chicken cutlets. 不要切 (don't cut it) and 要辣 (spicy) are common requests.

example.zh: 雞排不要切，要辣。
example.en: Don't cut the chicken cutlet, and make it spicy.

note: You choose items into a basket and they're simmered in a soy-based broth.

example.zh: 晚上買一點滷味回去吃。
example.en: Let's buy some braised snacks to eat at home tonight.

note: Fried with pickled cabbage (泡菜) or served 麻辣 in soup. 腐 keeps its full third tone in Taiwan.

example.zh: 你敢吃臭豆腐嗎？
example.en: Do you dare eat stinky tofu?

note: Shortened to 珍奶. 波霸 = large pearls.

example.zh: 我要一杯珍奶，半糖少冰。
example.en: I'd like a bubble tea, half sugar, less ice.

note: Umbrella term for drink shops and their drinks (茶, 奶茶, 果汁).

example.zh: 台灣的手搖飲店真的太多了。
example.en: There are honestly too many drink stands in Taiwan.

note: Sugar scale: 全糖 > 少糖 > 半糖 > 微糖 > 無糖. Say sugar then ice: 半糖少冰.

example.zh: 綠茶半糖去冰，謝謝。
example.en: Green tea, half sugar, no ice, thanks.

note: Ice scale: 正常冰 > 少冰 > 微冰 > 去冰 > 常溫 > 溫 > 熱.

example.zh: 我的要去冰。
example.en: Mine with no ice, please.

note: Casual places where most dishes cost about the same; good for groups and beer.

example.zh: 今天下班去熱炒喝一杯。
example.en: Let's go to a stir-fry place for a drink after work.

note: Taiwan names hot-pot styles with 鍋: 麻辣鍋, 小火鍋 (individual hot pot), 薑母鴨.

example.zh: 冬天就是要吃麻辣鍋。
example.en: Winter is all about spicy hot pot.

note: 逛夜市 = stroll around a night market. Famous ones: 士林, 饒河, 寧夏, 逢甲.

example.zh: 我們晚上去逛夜市吧。
example.en: Let's go walk around the night market tonight.

note: In Taiwan 開水 is any plain drinking water (冰開水 = iced water), not only hot boiled water. Many restaurants have free self-serve water.

example.zh: 不好意思，可以給我一杯冰開水嗎？
example.en: Excuse me, could I get a glass of iced water?

note: 叫外送 = order delivery; 外送員 = delivery rider (Uber Eats, foodpanda). 外賣 is understood but less used.

example.zh: 下雨天懶得出門，叫外送好了。
example.en: It's raining and I can't be bothered to go out, let's order delivery.

en: self-serve cafeteria (pay for what you take)
note: In Taiwan 自助餐 is a canteen where you scoop dishes and pay by the amount; an all-you-can-eat buffet is 吃到飽. On the mainland 自助餐 means a buffet.

example.zh: 中午去巷口的自助餐吃。
example.en: Let's eat at the cafeteria at the corner for lunch.

en: to pay the bill; to check out
note: At restaurants and stores. 買單 is understood, but 結帳 is the standard Taiwan word.

example.zh: 不好意思，我們要結帳。
example.en: Excuse me, we'd like to pay.

note: 服務員 sounds mainland. In practice people just call out 不好意思 to get attention.

example.zh: 服務生說飲料等一下就來。
example.en: The waiter said the drinks will be right out.

note: Short for 便利超商. You can pay bills, print, pick up parcels and buy train tickets there.

example.zh: 我去一下超商，你要不要喝什麼？
example.en: I'm popping to the convenience store, do you want a drink?

note: Full form of 超商. Mainland 便利店.

example.zh: 台灣的便利商店幾乎什麼都有。
example.en: Taiwan's convenience stores have almost everything.

note: Also just 7-11 or 'seven'. FamilyMart is 全家.

example.zh: 我在小七門口等你。
example.en: I'll wait for you in front of the 7-Eleven.

note: 新光三越, SOGO. Taiwanese say 去百貨公司 where mainlanders say 去商场. The big autumn sale is 週年慶.

example.zh: 百貨公司週年慶人超多。
example.en: The department-store anniversary sale is packed.

note: Every receipt doubles as a lottery ticket, drawn every two months (對發票 = check your receipts). On the mainland 发票 means a tax invoice.

example.zh: 發票要留著，說不定會中獎。
example.en: Keep your receipt, you might win.

note: Cashiers ask 有載具嗎？ — show your phone barcode to store the receipt digitally.

example.zh: 店員問我有沒有載具。
example.en: The cashier asked if I had an e-invoice barcode.

note: Taiwan 塑膠, mainland 塑料. Bags cost a few NT$; the cashier asks 要袋子嗎？

example.zh: 不用塑膠袋，謝謝。
example.en: No plastic bag, thanks.

note: From 'PET bottle'. Goes in 資源回收.

example.zh: 寶特瓶要洗乾淨再回收。
example.en: Rinse plastic bottles before recycling them.

note: Also 優惠券. 折 = discount.

example.zh: 用這張折價券可以便宜五十塊。
example.en: This coupon takes fifty dollars off.

note: Convenience-store sticker collecting (集點換公仔) is a national hobby.

example.zh: 我在集點換杯子。
example.en: I'm collecting points to get a cup.

note: 'Kill the price'. Fine at night markets and traditional markets, not in chain stores.

example.zh: 在夜市買衣服可以殺價看看。
example.en: You can try haggling when buying clothes at the night market.

note: 錢包 is also used, but 皮夾 is very common.

example.zh: 我的皮夾忘在計程車上了！
example.en: I left my wallet in the taxi!

note: From Japanese. 宅配到府 = delivered to your door. 快遞 in Taiwan usually means an express courier.

example.zh: 東西用宅配寄過去比較方便。
example.en: It's easier to send it by home delivery.

en: to pick up an online order at a convenience store
note: The default for online shopping in Taiwan; often 貨到付款 (pay on pickup).

example.zh: 我網購都選超商取貨。
example.en: I always choose convenience-store pickup when shopping online.

en: to pay by card; to tap a card
note: Same as the mainland, but in Taiwan you'll ask it constantly: 可以刷卡嗎？ Also used for tapping 悠遊卡.

example.zh: 請問可以刷卡嗎？
example.en: Can I pay by card?

note: 開冷氣 / 關冷氣; 冷氣好強 = the AC is really strong. 空調 is technical in Taiwan.

example.zh: 好熱喔，冷氣可以開強一點嗎？
example.en: It's so hot, can you turn the AC up?

note: Essential in humid Taiwan, especially in plum-rain season (梅雨季).

example.zh: 梅雨季一定要開除濕機。
example.en: You have to run the dehumidifier in plum-rain season.

note: From Japanese gasu. 瓦斯爐 = gas stove; 叫瓦斯 = order a gas canister delivery.

example.zh: 瓦斯好像沒了，洗澡都沒熱水。
example.en: I think the gas ran out, there's no hot water for the shower.

note: Covers both tissue and toilet paper. Older toilets have a sign asking you to put used paper in the bin; newer ones say to flush it.

example.zh: 你有衛生紙嗎？借我一張。
example.en: Do you have a tissue? Can I have one?

note: 垃圾 is read lè sè in Taiwan. Trucks play 'Für Elise' or 'A Maiden's Prayer', and you take your bags out to meet them (倒垃圾 / 追垃圾車).

example.zh: 垃圾車來了，快去倒垃圾！
example.en: The garbage truck's here, hurry and take out the trash!

note: Sorted strictly: 紙類, 寶特瓶, 鐵鋁罐, and food waste (廚餘) separately.

example.zh: 寶特瓶要丟資源回收。
example.en: Plastic bottles go in recycling.

note: Collected separately by the garbage truck.

example.zh: 廚餘要另外裝，不要跟一般垃圾混在一起。
example.en: Bag food waste separately, don't mix it with regular trash.

note: Rental terms: 套房 = own bathroom; 雅房 = shared bathroom; 整層 = whole apartment.

example.zh: 我在學校附近租了一間套房。
example.en: I rented a studio near school.

note: 租屋網 = rental website. 押金 = deposit, usually two months' rent.

example.zh: 在台北租屋真的很貴。
example.en: Renting in Taipei is really expensive.

en: townhouse (one family owns the whole building)
note: 厝 is Hokkien tshù 'house'. Common in central and southern Taiwan.

example.zh: 他們家是三層樓的透天厝。
example.en: Their home is a three-story townhouse.

note: Apartment buildings have a 管理員 at the front desk who signs for parcels.

example.zh: 包裹寄到管理員那邊就好。
example.en: Just have the parcel sent to the building's front desk.

note: The polite word; 廁所 is also perfectly normal.

example.zh: 請問洗手間在哪裡？
example.en: Excuse me, where's the restroom?

note: Taiwan says 原子筆. 子 keeps its full tone here.

example.zh: 可以借我一支原子筆嗎？
example.en: Can I borrow a pen?

note: A brand name turned generic. Correction tape is 立可帶.

example.zh: 寫錯了，用立可白塗掉就好。
example.en: If you write it wrong, just white it out.

note: In Taiwan 研究所 is a grad program (考研究所, 念研究所); on the mainland it means a research institute.

example.zh: 他大學畢業後去念研究所。
example.en: He went to grad school after college.

note: 學科能力測驗, held every January for high-school seniors.

example.zh: 她今年要考學測，壓力很大。
example.en: She's taking the GSAT this year, she's under a lot of pressure.

note: 指定科目考試; replaced in 2022 by 分科測驗, but anyone who took it still says 考指考.

example.zh: 我當年是考指考上大學的。
example.en: Back then I got into college through the July exam.

note: Huge in Taiwan: English, maths, exam prep. 去補習 = go to cram school.

example.zh: 他放學後還要去補習班。
example.en: After school he still has to go to cram school.

note: 國民小學. 國小三年級 = third grade.

example.zh: 我女兒今年上國小一年級。
example.en: My daughter is starting first grade this year.

note: 國民中學, ages 12–15. 初中 is not used in Taiwan.

example.zh: 我們是國中同學。
example.en: We were junior-high classmates.

note: Seniority terms are used a lot: 學長, 學姊 (Taiwan writes 姊, mainland 姐), 學弟, 學妹. Also used at work between alumni.

example.zh: 這位是我大學的學長。
example.en: This is my senior from college.

note: In school = homeroom teacher; in grad school a thesis advisor is 指導教授.

example.zh: 我們的導師很照顧學生。
example.en: Our homeroom teacher really looks after the students.

note: 發考卷 = hand out papers; 改考卷 = grade papers.

example.zh: 老師明天會發考卷。
example.en: The teacher will hand back the tests tomorrow.

note: 期 is qí in Taiwan. Finals are 期末考.

example.zh: 下禮拜就是期中考了。
example.en: Midterms are next week.

note: 被當 = got failed. 電腦當掉了 = the computer froze.

example.zh: 我微積分被當了。
example.en: I failed calculus.

note: 翹班 = skip work.

example.zh: 他今天又翹課了。
example.en: He skipped class again today.

note: 參加社團 = join a club. 社課 = club meeting.

example.zh: 你大學參加什麼社團？
example.en: What club were you in at college?

note: Taiwan's phonetic system (ㄅㄆㄇㄈ). Kids learn it first and many people type with it. Pinyin is used for romanised signs.

example.zh: 台灣小孩先學注音再學國字。
example.en: Taiwanese kids learn Zhuyin before characters.

note: Taiwanese call Mandarin 國語 or 中文; 普通話 sounds mainland.

example.zh: 他的國語有一點台灣腔。
example.en: His Mandarin has a bit of a Taiwanese accent.

note: The most widely spoken local language; 閩南語 is the formal or school name.

example.zh: 我阿嬤只會講台語。
example.en: My grandma only speaks Taiwanese.

note: In Taiwan 打工 means a student or part-time job (在超商打工). 打工度假 = working holiday. On the mainland 打工 suggests manual or migrant labour.

example.zh: 我大學的時候在飲料店打工。
example.en: In college I worked part-time at a drink shop.

note: The salaried class; 小資上班族 = modest earners.

example.zh: 很多上班族中午都吃便當。
example.en: Lots of office workers eat bento for lunch.

note: Everyday word; 領薪水 = get paid. 薪資 is formal. 工資 sounds blue-collar or mainland.

example.zh: 這個月的薪水還沒入帳。
example.en: This month's salary hasn't come in yet.

note: Also how you address a stall owner: 老闆，一碗麵！ For a woman: 老闆娘.

example.zh: 老闆，再來一碗！
example.en: Boss, another bowl please!

note: Taiwan offices say 主管; 領導 sounds political or mainland.

example.zh: 我要先問一下主管。
example.en: I need to check with my manager first.

note: 年終獎金, usually counted in months of salary: 年終兩個月.

example.zh: 今年年終領了三個月。
example.en: This year's bonus was three months' pay.

note: Held before Lunar New Year, with a prize draw (抽獎). The post-New-Year version is 春酒.

example.zh: 公司尾牙抽到一台電視！
example.en: I won a TV at the company year-end party!

note: 特別休假. 請特休 = take annual leave.

example.zh: 我下個月要請特休出國。
example.en: I'm taking annual leave next month to go abroad.

en: salaried role with no overtime pay
note: Often a complaint: 責任制 means unlimited unpaid overtime.

example.zh: 他的工作是責任制，常常加班到很晚。
example.en: His job has no overtime pay, he often works late.

note: 投履歷 = send in résumés; 104 is the big job site.

example.zh: 我已經投了十幾份履歷。
example.en: I've already sent out more than ten résumés.

note: In Taiwan 業務 often means a sales rep (跑業務); it also means 'line of business'.

example.zh: 他在保險公司當業務。
example.en: He works in sales at an insurance company.

note: 行銷企劃 = marketing planner. 企 is qì in Taiwan.

example.zh: 這份企劃明天要交。
example.en: This proposal is due tomorrow.

note: Compulsory for men; one year for those born in 2005 or later. 當兵的時候… is a classic male conversation topic.

example.zh: 他明年要去當兵。
example.en: He's doing his military service next year.

note: 全民健保 makes doctor visits very cheap. 健保有給付嗎？ = Does NHI cover it?

example.zh: 這個檢查健保有給付。
example.en: National Health Insurance covers this test.

note: Bring it to every clinic: the receptionist will say 健保卡給我.

example.zh: 看醫生記得帶健保卡。
example.en: Remember your health insurance card when you see a doctor.

note: 網路掛號 = book online; 掛號費 = registration fee. 掛號信 = registered mail.

example.zh: 我已經在網路上掛號了。
example.en: I already booked online.

en: (of a doctor) to see patients; consultation
note: Clinic signs: 看診時間 = consulting hours. As a patient you usually say 看醫生.

example.zh: 這家診所晚上也有看診。
example.en: This clinic sees patients in the evenings too.

note: Small neighbourhood clinics are where most people go first (耳鼻喉科, 牙醫診所).

example.zh: 我去巷口的診所看一下感冒。
example.en: I'll get my cold seen at the clinic down the street.

note: Taiwan 藥局 or 藥房; mainland 药店.

example.zh: 去藥局買個口罩。
example.en: Go buy some masks at the pharmacy.

note: Short for 健康檢查.

example.zh: 公司每年都安排員工健檢。
example.en: The company arranges a check-up for staff every year.

note: Mainland 卫生巾; Taiwan 衛生棉.

example.zh: 超商就買得到衛生棉。
example.en: You can buy sanitary pads at convenience stores.

note: 去做復健 = go to physio; 復健科 = rehabilitation department.

example.zh: 他膝蓋受傷，每個禮拜都要去復健。
example.en: He hurt his knee and goes to physio every week.

note: 掛急診 = go to the ER.

example.zh: 他半夜發高燒，被送去急診。
example.en: He had a high fever at midnight and was taken to the ER.

note: Taiwan writes 身分 (mainland 身份). 身分證字號 = ID number.

example.zh: 辦手機門號要帶身分證。
example.en: You need your ID card to get a phone number.

note: Foreigners' residence card. 移民署 = immigration agency.

example.zh: 我的居留證下個月到期。
example.en: My ARC expires next month.

note: Local government office in each 區. Household registration is handled at the 戶政事務所.

example.zh: 補助要去區公所申請。
example.en: Apply for the subsidy at the district office.

note: The most local elected official; affectionately 里長伯. 里 is the smallest administrative unit.

example.zh: 這件事可以找里長幫忙。
example.en: You can ask the neighbourhood chief for help with this.

note: Short for 立法委員, member of the 立法院 (Legislative Yuan).

example.zh: 立委選舉快到了。
example.en: The legislative election is coming up.

note: 總統府 = Presidential Office Building.

example.zh: 總統大選四年一次。
example.en: The presidential election is every four years.

note: Where you 考駕照 (take a driving test) and register vehicles.

example.zh: 我明天要去監理站考機車駕照。
example.en: I'm taking my scooter licence test at the DMV tomorrow.

note: In speech prices are just 塊 or 元: 一百塊.

example.zh: 這杯咖啡八十塊新台幣。
example.en: This coffee is 80 NT dollars.

note: Every convenience store has one. 領錢 = withdraw cash; the card is a 提款卡.

example.zh: 我先去提款機領個錢。
example.en: I'll get some cash from the ATM first.

note: 銅板價 = very cheap (a few coins' worth).

example.zh: 這家麵店是銅板價，很划算。
example.en: This noodle shop only costs a few coins, a great deal.

note: From 'cartoon'. Japanese anime is 動漫 or 動畫.

example.zh: 小時候每天放學都在看卡通。
example.en: As a kid I watched cartoons every day after school.

note: Western series are often 影集. 追劇 = follow or binge a show.

example.zh: 我媽每天晚上都在看連續劇。
example.en: My mom watches TV dramas every night.

note: Taiwan's 2000s genre (流星花園 and many more). 很偶像劇 = cheesily romantic.

example.zh: 這個情節也太偶像劇了吧。
example.en: This plot is way too idol-drama.

note: 綜 is zòng in Taiwan.

example.zh: 週末晚上都是綜藝節目。
example.en: Weekend evenings are all variety shows.

note: 被狗仔拍到 = caught by the paparazzi.

example.zh: 他跟女朋友約會被狗仔拍到了。
example.en: He got snapped by paparazzi on a date with his girlfriend.

note: Taiwan film titles often differ completely from mainland ones; many Hollywood titles start with 神鬼 (神鬼戰士 Gladiator, 神鬼交鋒 Catch Me If You Can).

example.zh: 神鬼奇航又出續集了。
example.en: There's another Pirates of the Caribbean sequel.

note: Taiwan transliterates foreign names differently, e.g. 歐巴馬 (mainland 奥巴马) for Obama.

example.zh: 新聞一直在報川普的消息。
example.en: The news keeps reporting on Trump.

note: 'Lazy-person pack': a summary of a complicated issue.

example.zh: 有人整理了一個懶人包，看完就懂了。
example.en: Someone made an explainer, read it and you'll get it.

note: From 業務配合. 這是業配吧？ = this is an ad, right?

example.zh: 這支影片一看就是業配。
example.en: This video is obviously sponsored.

note: From PTT forum culture ('villagers'). 網友 is the neutral word.

example.zh: 鄉民的反應都很激烈。
example.en: Netizens reacted really strongly.

note: Family-run guesthouses, common in 花蓮, 墾丁, 九份.

example.zh: 我們在花蓮訂了一間民宿。
example.en: We booked a guesthouse in Hualien.

note: Use 飯店 for hotels in Taiwan. 酒店 can mean a hostess club, so be careful.

example.zh: 我們住的飯店離車站很近。
example.en: Our hotel is close to the station.

en: to travel around the island of Taiwan
note: By bike, scooter or train; something of a rite of passage.

example.zh: 我畢業的時候騎腳踏車環島。
example.en: When I graduated I cycled around the island.

en: to soak in a hot spring
note: 北投, 礁溪, 烏來. Also slang: 計畫泡湯了 = the plan fell through.

example.zh: 冬天最適合去北投泡湯。
example.en: Winter is the best time to soak in Beitou's hot springs.

note: Bringing 伴手禮 back for coworkers after a trip is expected.

example.zh: 出國記得買伴手禮給同事。
example.en: Remember to buy souvenirs for your coworkers when you travel.

note: Taiwan transliteration.

example.zh: 他去紐西蘭打工度假一年。
example.en: He went to New Zealand on a one-year working holiday.

note: Same characters as the fruit; context makes it clear.

example.zh: 我表姊住在雪梨。
example.en: My cousin lives in Sydney.

note: Taiwan nearly always says 澳洲.

example.zh: 很多年輕人去澳洲打工度假。
example.en: Lots of young people go to Australia on working holidays.

note: Taiwan writes 義; also 義式咖啡 = espresso drinks.

example.zh: 我好想去義大利玩。
example.en: I really want to travel to Italy.

en: to worship (at a temple or for ancestors)
note: Not the same as 掰掰 (bye-bye). 去廟裡拜拜 = go pray at the temple.

example.zh: 過年要去廟裡拜拜。
example.en: At New Year we go to pray at the temple.

note: The most popular deity in Taiwan; the 大甲媽祖遶境 is a huge annual pilgrimage.

example.zh: 每年都有很多人跟著媽祖遶境。
example.en: Every year many people join the Mazu pilgrimage.

note: Taboos: don't swim, don't whistle at night, avoid moving house. Shops set out offerings for 中元普渡.

example.zh: 鬼月不要去游泳。
example.en: Don't go swimming during Ghost Month.

note: In Ghost Month people avoid saying 鬼 directly. Otherwise it just means close buddies.

example.zh: 鬼月要拜好兄弟。
example.en: During Ghost Month you make offerings to the 'good brothers'.

en: to see in the New Year
note: 台北101 fireworks; 跨年晚會 = New Year's Eve concert.

example.zh: 今年要去哪裡跨年？
example.en: Where are you going for New Year's Eve this year?

note: Communities built for soldiers' families after 1949; 眷村菜 is its own food style.

example.zh: 他是在眷村長大的。
example.en: He grew up in a military dependents' village.

note: Very common in Taiwan speech: 禮拜一, 下禮拜, 禮拜天. 星期 (read xīng qí in Taiwan) is equally fine.

example.zh: 我們下禮拜三見。
example.en: See you next Wednesday.

note: The most common Taiwanese 'OK'. 喔 makes it warm and friendly; a bare 好 can sound curt.

example.zh: 「明天七點見？」「好喔！」
example.en: 'See you at seven tomorrow?' 'Sure!'

note: Short for 真的假的. Pure surprise, not doubt.

example.zh: 「他們分手了。」「真假？」
example.en: 'They broke up.' 'No way!'

note: When something is so unexpected or absurd you just stare. Playful extension: 傻眼貓咪.

example.zh: 看到帳單我整個傻眼。
example.en: I was totally stunned when I saw the bill.

note: Also 好扯, 太扯了. For outrageous situations or claims.

example.zh: 一碗麵要四百塊？也太扯了吧！
example.en: Four hundred for a bowl of noodles? That's ridiculous!

note: Constantly used before adjectives and verbs: 超好吃, 超累, 超想去. More common in Taiwan than mainland 特別 / 賊.

example.zh: 這家的鬆餅超好吃！
example.en: This place's waffles are super good!

note: 讚 = great (also a Facebook 'like'). Thumbs up and 讚！ is a common reaction.

example.zh: 你的報告做得超讚！
example.en: Your presentation was awesome!

note: For something silly or pointless, often with an eye-roll. Slightly milder than 很扯.

example.zh: 這個理由也太瞎了吧。
example.en: That excuse is so lame.

note: From Hokkien pe̍h-ba̍k ('white eyes'). For someone who can't read the room. 你很白目耶 is a real criticism, though often said jokingly between friends.

example.zh: 他在喪禮上講笑話，真的很白目。
example.en: He told jokes at the funeral, so tactless.

note: Same word as 'scooter', but 你很機車 = you're being a pain. 機車的老闆 = a difficult boss. Mild, but not for elders.

example.zh: 那個客人真的很機車，一直挑毛病。
example.en: That customer was a real pain, nitpicking nonstop.

note: 好糗 = so embarrassing; 出糗 = embarrass oneself; 糗事 = embarrassing story.

example.zh: 我在台上跌倒，好糗喔。
example.en: I tripped on stage, so embarrassing.

note: The character is the Hokkien word giâ ('to lift, raise'); in Mandarin slang it's read hāng. 最夯的 = the hottest.

example.zh: 這家店最近很夯，要排很久。
example.en: This shop is really hot right now, the line is long.

en: to stay at home; geeky, homebody
note: From Japanese otaku. 很宅 = homebody; 宅在家 = hole up at home.

example.zh: 我放假都宅在家打電動。
example.en: On holidays I just stay home playing video games.

note: Can be self-deprecating or teasing. Female version 宅女.

example.zh: 他是標準的宅男，每天都在看動漫。
example.en: He's a classic otaku, watching anime every day.

note: 正 = hot, good-looking (很正). Common, a bit laddish.

example.zh: 你們公司是不是很多正妹？
example.en: Aren't there lots of pretty girls at your company?

note: Vendors call male customers 帥哥 and female ones 美女 regardless of looks.

example.zh: 帥哥，要不要試吃看看？
example.en: Hey handsome, want to try a sample?

note: Popular in the 2000s; now sounds a bit dated or cheesy.

example.zh: 那家飲料店的美眉很親切。
example.en: The girl at that drink shop is really friendly.

note: From Haruki Murakami; hugely popular in Taiwan for everyday small joys.

example.zh: 下班買一杯珍奶就是我的小確幸。
example.en: Getting a bubble tea after work is my little happiness.

en: to round up a group (for an activity or group buy)
note: 揪 = gather people. 揪團買 = group purchase; 有人要揪嗎？

example.zh: 我們揪團去墾丁玩吧！
example.en: Let's round up a group and go to Kenting!

note: The Taiwan word for a buffet (mainland 自助餐). Also for unlimited data plans: 網路吃到飽.

example.zh: 這家燒肉吃到飽一個人六百。
example.en: This all-you-can-eat BBQ is 600 per person.

note: At the end of a meal: 可以幫我打包嗎？ Also means packing luggage.

example.zh: 這些吃不完，我們打包吧。
example.en: We can't finish this, let's take it to go.

note: Shops always ask 內用還是外帶？ (eat in or take away?).

example.zh: 「內用還是外帶？」「外帶，謝謝。」
example.en: 'For here or to go?' 'To go, thanks.'

note: Opposite of 外帶.

example.zh: 我們內用，兩位。
example.en: We'll eat here, two people.

note: From Hokkien lû (to pester). 你很盧耶 = you're being so persistent/annoying. 盧小小 = nag a little.

example.zh: 他一直盧我陪他去看電影。
example.en: He kept pestering me to go to the movie with him.

note: From Hokkien ku-mn̂g ('turtle hair'). For people who take forever over tiny details.

example.zh: 他很龜毛，買一支筆要考慮半天。
example.en: He's so fussy, he takes ages to decide on a pen.

note: 很雷 = terrible (movie, restaurant, teammate); 雷片 = a bad film. Also 有雷 = contains spoilers.

example.zh: 這部電影很雷，不要去看。
example.en: This film is awful, don't bother.

en: to pick a dud ('step on a mine')
note: Ordering a bad dish, buying a bad product, picking a bad restaurant.

example.zh: 這家餐廳評價很好，結果還是踩雷了。
example.en: This restaurant had great reviews, but it was still a dud.

note: 不要爆雷！ = no spoilers! Posts are marked 有雷 or 防雷.

example.zh: 我還沒看完，你不要爆雷！
example.en: I haven't finished it yet, no spoilers!

note: Written with Zhuyin because the syllable 'kiang' doesn't exist in Mandarin; the pinyin here is only an approximation. For someone acting goofy or weird.

example.zh: 他今天很ㄎㄧㄤ，一直講奇怪的笑話。
example.en: He's being so wacky today, telling weird jokes nonstop.

note: For something so silly it feels like trolling. 你很鬧耶 = you're messing around. 不要鬧了 = stop it.

example.zh: 這個新聞標題也太鬧了吧。
example.en: That news headline is absurd.

note: Vulgar. A Mandarin spelling of Hokkien siánn-siâu. Recognise it, but don't say it unless you're very close with someone.

example.zh: 你在講啥小？
example.en: What the f*** are you talking about?

en: damn it; to whine, bitch about
note: Vulgar, from Hokkien khàu-pē ('cry for your father'). 靠北！ = damn!; 靠北老闆 = complain about the boss. 靠北 pages are anonymous rant pages.

example.zh: 他整天在靠北工作。
example.en: He bitches about work all day.

note: Vulgar. From Hokkien kàn; the most common swear word in Taiwan. Very strong in front of elders or strangers.

example.zh: 幹，我手機忘在車上了！
example.en: F***, I left my phone in the car!

note: A clipped, milder form; still not for formal settings. 哇靠 = whoa, holy crap.

example.zh: 靠，又下雨了。
example.en: Damn, it's raining again.

note: Surprise or amazement. Casual, among friends.

example.zh: 哇靠，你中樂透喔？
example.en: Whoa, did you win the lottery?

note: The Taiwan response to 謝謝 or 不好意思. Mainland speakers tend to say 不客氣 / 没事.

example.zh: 「謝謝你幫忙。」「不會啦！」
example.en: 'Thanks for helping.' 'No problem!'

en: it's OK, don't worry about it
note: 啦 makes it reassuring. Note 係 keeps its fourth tone in Taiwan.

example.zh: 沒關係啦，下次再約。
example.en: It's fine, let's make plans another time.

note: Said to coworkers at the end of the day, to delivery workers, to someone who just finished a task. Not sarcastic.

example.zh: 今天大家辛苦了，早點回家休息。
example.en: Thanks for your hard work today everyone, go home and rest.

note: The all-purpose Taiwan politeness word: getting attention, asking for something, small apologies. Used far more than 對不起.

example.zh: 不好意思，請問捷運站怎麼走？
example.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the MRT station?

en: good luck! you can do it!
note: Encouragement before exams, games or hard tasks. Also literally 'refuel'.

example.zh: 明天考試加油！
example.en: Good luck on your exam tomorrow!

en: inexplicable, makes no sense; out of nowhere
note: Very common in Taiwan for irritation at weird behaviour: 他很莫名其妙.

example.zh: 他莫名其妙就生氣了。
example.en: He got angry out of nowhere.

note: Can sound dismissive or annoyed. To be polite say 都可以 instead.

example.zh: 「晚餐吃什麼？」「隨便。」
example.en: 'What do you want for dinner?' 'Whatever.'

note: The polite answer to a choice. Taiwanese use it a lot (sometimes frustratingly).

example.zh: 「要吃中式還是日式？」「都可以啊。」
example.en: 'Chinese or Japanese food?' 'Either is fine.'

note: Hands the decision back. Also 看你方便 = whatever suits you.

example.zh: 時間看你，我都有空。
example.en: You pick the time, I'm free whenever.

note: Short for 沒有差別. 差 is chā here.

example.zh: 早一點晚一點都沒差。
example.en: A bit earlier or later makes no difference.

note: From English 'bye-bye'; written 掰掰 to separate it from 拜拜 (worship). Also 掰.

example.zh: 掰掰，到家跟我說一聲。
example.en: Bye, let me know when you get home.

note: Ending a phone call or chat: 那先這樣，掰掰. Also 先這樣吧.

example.zh: 好，那我們先這樣，有問題再說。
example.en: OK, let's leave it there; we'll talk if anything comes up.

note: How people leave the office or a gathering. Reply: 慢走 or 掰掰.

example.zh: 大家辛苦了，我先走囉！
example.en: Thanks everyone, I'm heading off!

note: Said by a host or shopkeeper as you leave. Also 謝謝光臨 in shops.

example.zh: 謝謝你來，慢走喔。
example.en: Thanks for coming, take care.

note: What servers say as they put food down.

example.zh: 您的牛肉麵，請慢用。
example.en: Here's your beef noodle soup, enjoy.

note: Polite refusal of an offer (bag, receipt, help). Add 謝謝.

example.zh: 「要袋子嗎？」「不用了，謝謝。」
example.en: 'Do you need a bag?' 'No thanks.'

note: Correct but a little formal; 不會 / 不會啦 is more common in casual Taiwan speech. 氣 keeps its tone (kè qì).

example.zh: 「謝謝老師。」「不客氣。」
example.en: 'Thank you, teacher.' 'You're welcome.'

en: could you please…; sorry to trouble you
note: Very Taiwanese politeness: 麻煩你幫我… / 麻煩了. 煩 keeps its tone.

example.zh: 麻煩你幫我拿一下那個。
example.en: Could you pass me that, please?

note: For squeezing past people on the MRT or in a crowd.

example.zh: 不好意思，借過一下。
example.en: Excuse me, can I get past?

note: 改天請你吃飯 is often a polite formula, not a firm plan.

example.zh: 今天不行耶，改天好了。
example.en: Today doesn't work, let's do another day.

note: 約吃飯 = make plans to eat; 有約 = have plans; 要不要約？ = want to hang out?

example.zh: 我們禮拜六約看電影吧。
example.en: Let's plan a movie on Saturday.

note: With colleagues, classmates or a club.

example.zh: 公司下禮拜五要聚餐。
example.en: The company is having a dinner next Friday.

en: to move on to the next spot (after a meal/drinks)
note: 攤 = stall/round. 第二攤 = the second round (often KTV).

example.zh: 吃完飯要不要去KTV續攤？
example.en: Want to carry on at KTV after dinner?

note: 幫他慶生 = celebrate his birthday.

example.zh: 我們明天幫小美慶生。
example.en: We're celebrating Xiaomei's birthday tomorrow.

note: Guests bring a 紅包 (cash gift). 什麼時候請我們喝喜酒？ = When are you getting married?

example.zh: 這個週末要回南部喝喜酒。
example.en: This weekend I'm going down south for a wedding banquet.

note: Also 我請你 / 這頓我請. Expect some polite fighting over the bill.

example.zh: 今天我請客，大家不要跟我搶。
example.en: It's my treat today, nobody fight me for it.

en: to split the bill (each pays their own)
note: Mainland slang AA制 is understood too.

example.zh: 我們各付各的就好。
example.en: Let's just each pay for our own.

note: Pleading (拜託你啦！) or exasperated (拜託，怎麼可能！).

example.zh: 拜託，幫我一下啦！
example.en: Please, help me out!

en: come off it, give me a break
note: Dismissing a claim or flattery.

example.zh: 少來，你明明就很喜歡她。
example.en: Come off it, you obviously like her.

note: Between friends. Also 感謝, 3Q (spoken 'sank you') online.

example.zh: 謝啦，下次請你喝飲料。
example.en: Thanks, I'll buy you a drink next time.

en: it's nothing; never mind; I'm fine
note: Answering 你怎麼了？ or cancelling a question: 沒事，我自己來.

example.zh: 「你還好嗎？」「沒事，只是有點累。」
example.en: 'Are you OK?' 'I'm fine, just a bit tired.'

note: Relief after a near miss.

example.zh: 好險有帶傘，不然就淋濕了。
example.en: Good thing I brought an umbrella, or I'd be soaked.

note: Also 嚇我一跳 (startled me).

example.zh: 你突然出現，嚇死我了！
example.en: You appeared out of nowhere, you scared me to death!

note: Typed and said: 笑死，太好笑了. Also 笑到肚子痛.

example.zh: 笑死，你這張照片也太醜了吧。
example.en: LOL, this photo of you is so ugly.

note: 你很煩耶 = you're so annoying (often teasing). 煩死了 = so annoying.

example.zh: 工作的事情很煩，不想講。
example.en: Work stuff is a pain, I don't want to talk about it.

en: to lose it, be at one's wits' end
note: Exaggerated daily use: 我要崩潰了 = I'm going crazy.

example.zh: 報告明天要交，我快崩潰了。
example.en: The report is due tomorrow, I'm about to lose it.

note: A very Taiwanese reaction to someone's good news; means 'how nice for you'.

example.zh: 「我下禮拜要去日本。」「好好喔！」
example.en: 'I'm going to Japan next week.' 'Lucky you!'

note: Impressed: 這個技術太狂了. Also for bold people.

example.zh: 他一個人騎機車環島，很狂。
example.en: He rode a scooter around the island by himself, that's wild.

note: 很神 / 神人 (a genius at something) / 神回覆 (a brilliant reply).

example.zh: 他三分鐘就修好了，真的很神。
example.en: He fixed it in three minutes, he's amazing.

note: Vulgar origin (slang for penis), but used as 'cool': 很屌. Avoid in polite company.

example.zh: 你那台車也太屌了吧！
example.en: Your car is so badass!

note: Can be affectionate (他很白爛 = he's a goofball) or critical (a dumb comment).

example.zh: 他很白爛，常常講一些無聊的笑話。
example.en: He's a goofball, always telling silly jokes.

note: For anything extreme: 人多到很誇張 = crazy crowded.

example.zh: 過年的時候高速公路塞得很誇張。
example.en: The freeway gets insanely jammed over New Year.

note: PTT-era praise for a fair take. 中 is zhòng (hitting the mark).

example.zh: 你這個評論很中肯。
example.en: Your comment is spot on.

note: From PTT upvotes. 大推 = highly recommend; 推薦 is the full word.

example.zh: 這家拉麵大推！
example.en: I highly recommend this ramen place!

en: read but didn't reply (left on read)
note: From LINE's 已讀 read receipt. A common relationship complaint.

example.zh: 她已讀不回，是不是生氣了？
example.en: She left me on read, is she angry?

note: 網美 = influencer-style girl; 網美店 / 網美景點 = places designed for photos.

example.zh: 這家咖啡廳是網美店，大家都來拍照。
example.en: This café is an Instagram spot, everyone comes to take photos.

note: From 酸 (sarcastic, mean) + 民. Mainland 喷子.

example.zh: 不要理那些酸民。
example.en: Ignore the trolls.

note: 酸他 = take a dig at him; 酸言酸語 = snide comments.

example.zh: 他一直在酸我，很討厭。
example.en: He keeps taking digs at me, it's annoying.

en: to roast, call out, make fun of
note: From Japanese tsukkomi via Taiwan. Now used on the mainland too.

example.zh: 大家都在吐槽這部電影的結局。
example.en: Everyone's roasting the ending of this movie.

note: 嗆聲 = shout defiance; 很嗆 = aggressive, cheeky.

example.zh: 他在網路上嗆政府。
example.en: He was mouthing off at the government online.

note: Liver explosion: the Taiwanese belief that staying up late damages the liver.

example.zh: 為了趕專案，這禮拜每天都爆肝。
example.en: To finish the project I've been working myself ragged every day this week.

note: Usually after a big spend: 這個月要吃土了.

example.zh: 買了新手機，這個月只能吃土了。
example.en: I bought a new phone, so I'll be broke this month.

note: 小資族 / 小資女; 小資省錢術 = budgeting tips.

example.zh: 這家餐廳很適合小資族。
example.en: This restaurant is great for people on a budget.

note: Self-description for lazy days: 今天只想耍廢. 很廢 = useless, lazy.

example.zh: 放假就在家耍廢一整天。
example.en: On days off I laze around at home all day.

note: 擺臭臉 = put on a sour face.

example.zh: 店員一直擺臭臉，服務很差。
example.en: The clerk kept scowling, terrible service.

note: When something unfair or a missed chance leaves you fuming. 嘔 is ǒu.

example.zh: 差一分就及格，真的很嘔。
example.en: Missing a pass by one point is so galling.

note: Casual and fairly direct. 爽 alone = great, satisfying (很爽).

example.zh: 他講話那個態度讓我很不爽。
example.en: His attitude really pissed me off.

note: Often self-mocking: 我是邊緣人.

example.zh: 聚會的時候我都是邊緣人。
example.en: At parties I'm always the loner.

note: A pun on English 'loser'; often self-deprecating.

example.zh: 我就是個沒女朋友的魯蛇。
example.en: I'm just a loser with no girlfriend.

note: 他是我的天菜 = he's exactly my type.

example.zh: 那個新同事根本是我的天菜。
example.en: That new coworker is totally my type.

note: Literally 'seasick'. Common in dating talk.

example.zh: 才約一次會你就暈船了喔？
example.en: One date and you've already fallen for him?

en: to confess one's feelings (to a crush)
note: From Japanese kokuhaku. 被告白 = be confessed to.

example.zh: 他終於跟她告白了。
example.en: He finally told her how he feels.

note: Literally 'do the splits' (two partners at once).

example.zh: 他被發現劈腿，女朋友氣死了。
example.en: He got caught cheating, his girlfriend was furious.

note: 閃 = dazzle; 閃光 = one's partner or a lovey-dovey couple.

example.zh: 他們每天在網路上放閃。
example.en: They show off their relationship online every day.

note: A dating red flag in Taiwan.

example.zh: 他什麼都要問媽媽，根本是媽寶。
example.en: He asks his mom about everything, total mama's boy.

note: Older Taiwanese label for young workers seen as fragile.

example.zh: 不要動不動就說年輕人是草莓族。
example.en: Don't keep calling young people the 'strawberry generation'.

note: 把我當塑膠 = acting like I'm not even there.

example.zh: 你們聊得那麼開心，把我當塑膠喔？
example.en: You're chatting away, am I invisible or what?

note: 醬 is a slurred 這樣; mostly in text messages.

example.zh: 明天十點集合，就醬。
example.en: Meet at ten tomorrow, that's it.

en: very Taiwanese (often: folksy, a bit tacky)
note: Playful; can be proud or teasing (藍白拖 and 檳榔攤 are 很台). Example of 很 + noun.

example.zh: 穿藍白拖去吃熱炒，真的很台。
example.en: Wearing blue-and-white slippers to a stir-fry place, so Taiwanese.

en: pretty good, not bad at all
note: Approval: 這家咖啡很可以.

example.zh: 這個價錢有這個品質，很可以。
example.en: This quality at this price is pretty great.

en: (particle) friendly softener; gentle reminder or warning
note: Everywhere in Taiwan speech. Softens statements (好喔), adds a friendly reminder (要小心喔), or signals mild surprise as a question (喔？). Mainland speakers use 哦 more; Taiwanese write 喔.

example.zh: 明天要早起喔，不要太晚睡。
example.en: You have to get up early tomorrow, don't stay up too late.

note: Quick acknowledgement while listening or reading a message. A single flat 喔 can sound cold in text; 喔喔 or 好喔 is friendlier.

example.zh: 「會議改到三點。」「喔喔，好。」
example.en: 'The meeting moved to three.' 'Oh OK, got it.'

en: (particle) right? / ugh (seeking agreement or mild exasperation)
note: Very Taiwanese, from Hokkien. At the end it asks for agreement (很熱齁？ = hot, huh?); at the start it shows exasperation (齁～你很煩耶). Often also written 吼.

example.zh: 今天真的很熱齁？
example.en: It's really hot today, huh?

note: Spelling commonly used online for the same sound as 齁, especially at the start of a complaint or teasing scold.

example.zh: 吼，你又忘記帶鑰匙了！
example.en: Ugh, you forgot your keys again!

en: (particle) casual emphasis; reassurance, urging, brushing off
note: Makes speech relaxed or insistent: 好啦 (fine), 走啦 (come on, let's go), 不會啦 (not at all), 不要啦 (nah, don't). Used much more in Taiwan than on the mainland.

example.zh: 不會啦，你想太多了。
example.en: Nah, you're overthinking it.

note: At the start, 'hey' (欸，你看！). At the end, it marks surprise or emphasis, like 耶 (這個很好吃欸). Intonation varies; online it's often written ㄟ.

example.zh: 欸，你看那邊！
example.en: Hey, look over there!

note: Softens and adds feeling: 好漂亮耶, 我不知道耶 (hmm, I don't know). Very common in Taiwan; rare on the mainland.

example.zh: 我不知道耶，你問他看看。
example.en: Hmm, I don't know, try asking him.

note: 1) Like 呢: 你咧？ (and you?). 2) Rebuttal or emphasis: 才不咧 (no way), 我在忙咧 (I'm busy, you know).

example.zh: 我要喝咖啡，你咧？
example.en: I'm having coffee, what about you?

note: Marks something as obvious (就跟你說了嘛 = I told you so) or coaxes (一起去嘛 = come on, come with us).

example.zh: 一起去嘛，人多比較好玩。
example.en: Come on, come with us, it's more fun with more people.

note: Announces a new situation in a friendly way: 吃飯囉 (dinner's ready), 走囉 (let's go), 那我先掛囉 (I'll hang up now). Often sounds like 'lo'.

example.zh: 吃飯囉！大家快來。
example.en: Dinner's ready! Come on, everyone.

note: Rising tone. Asking someone to repeat, or reacting in disbelief (蛤？真的嗎？). Can sound rude to elders; 什麼？ or 不好意思，再說一次？ is safer.

example.zh: 蛤？你說什麼？我沒聽到。
example.en: Huh? What did you say? I didn't catch it.

note: A cuter 喔, common in service talk and texting: 要準時唷.

example.zh: 記得要準時唷！
example.en: Remember to be on time!

note: Short 'yeah' in answer to a yes-no question, from Hokkien (see 嘿啊). Also a greeting.

example.zh: 「你是台南人喔？」「嘿，對啊。」
example.en: 'You're from Tainan?' 'Yeah, that's right.'

note: The default agreement and backchannel in conversation, often repeated: 對啊對啊.

example.zh: 「這家店很好吃。」「對啊，我很常來。」
example.en: 'This place is really good.' 'Yeah, I come here a lot.'

note: Strong agreement, often 就是說啊！ Also introduces a rephrasing: 'that is to say'.

example.zh: 「房租也太貴了吧！」「就是說啊！」
example.en: 'Rent is way too expensive!' 'I know, right?'

note: Taiwanese speakers chain stories with 然後… 然後…; it often just fills a pause rather than meaning 'after that'.

example.zh: 我昨天去夜市，然後遇到我國中同學。
example.en: I went to the night market yesterday, and ran into my junior-high classmate.

note: Fills pauses and softens awkward requests. Often pronounced nèi ge in speech.

example.zh: 那個…我可以請一天假嗎？
example.en: Um… could I take a day off?

note: Very frequent; used to soften disagreement or add a gentle correction.

example.zh: 其實我不太喜歡吃辣。
example.en: Actually, I don't really like spicy food.

note: Wraps up or brushes aside details: 反正就是這樣.

example.zh: 反正明天放假，今天晚點睡沒關係。
example.en: Anyway, tomorrow's a holiday, so it's fine to stay up late.

note: Cheerful acceptance of an invitation. Compare 好啦 (fine, OK, reluctantly) and 好喔 (sure, warm).

example.zh: 「要不要一起吃飯？」「好啊！」
example.en: 'Want to eat together?' 'Sure!'

note: Concession or ending an argument: 好啦好啦，我去. Can also soothe: 好啦，不要哭了.

example.zh: 好啦好啦，我陪你去。
example.en: Fine, fine, I'll go with you.

note: Backchannel reaction to news. Falling tone = 'oh, I see'; rising = 'really?'. A flat 是喔 can sound uninterested, so add enthusiasm.

example.zh: 「我下個月要搬家。」「是喔？搬去哪？」
example.en: 'I'm moving next month.' 'Oh really? Where to?'

note: Surprised reaction, not a real question. Shortened to 真假.

example.zh: 真的假的？他要結婚了？
example.en: Seriously? He's getting married?

note: The modest reply to compliments, and a soft denial.

example.zh: 「你中文好好喔！」「沒有啦，還差很遠。」
example.en: 'Your Chinese is so good!' 'Nah, I've got a long way to go.'

note: 這樣子喔 = 'oh, I see'. Also 'like this' when demonstrating. Taiwanese often add 子.

example.zh: 「他今天請病假。」「這樣子喔。」
example.en: 'He's off sick today.' 'Oh, I see.'

note: Heavily used filler at the start of explanations, often without much meaning.

example.zh: 基本上我們禮拜一到五都有營業。
example.en: Basically we're open Monday to Friday.

note: Fills pauses or introduces a clarification: 就是…怎麼說…

example.zh: 就是…我覺得這個計畫有點問題。
example.en: I mean… I think there's a bit of a problem with this plan.

note: Introduces news or gossip. Taiwan uses 跟 here, not 和.

example.zh: 我跟你說，他們兩個在一起了！
example.en: Let me tell you, those two are dating now!

note: Buys time while choosing words: 怎麼說呢…

example.zh: 怎麼說呢，這部電影還不錯，可是有點長。
example.en: How should I put it… the film's decent, but a bit long.

note: In stories it introduces an unexpected outcome.

example.zh: 我等了一個小時，結果他沒來。
example.en: I waited an hour, and in the end he didn't show up.

note: Taiwanese often use 不然 to suggest an alternative: 不然我們改天？

example.zh: 不然我們改吃火鍋好了？
example.en: How about we have hot pot instead?

note: Draws a conclusion, sometimes with an 'I told you so' tone.

example.zh: 所以說，早點出門就不會遲到了。
example.en: So you see, if you'd left earlier you wouldn't be late.

note: Seeks confirmation. Softer variants: 對吧, 齁.

example.zh: 你是上禮拜來的，對不對？
example.en: You came last week, right?

note: Rising tone when answering the phone. Said to a person face-to-face (falling) it is rude, like 'hey you'.

example.zh: 喂？請問是王先生嗎？
example.en: Hello? Is this Mr Wang?

note: Introduces something you suddenly remembered.

example.zh: 欸對，你明天有空嗎？
example.en: Oh right, are you free tomorrow?

note: Signals sincerity or a frank opinion.

example.zh: 說真的，我覺得你應該跟他談談。
example.en: Honestly, I think you should talk to him.

note: Taiwanese hedge opinions with 我覺得 constantly; it sounds less blunt than stating things directly.

example.zh: 我覺得這件比較適合你。
example.en: I think this one suits you better.

en: what's up? / so what? (can be confrontational)
note: Neutral: 最近怎樣？ (how's it going?). Confrontational: 你想怎樣？ / 怎樣？ (what do you want?).

example.zh: 最近怎樣？工作還順利嗎？
example.en: How've you been? Is work going OK?

note: Amazement or surprise. 哇塞 is a stronger, older variant.

example.zh: 哇，這裡的夜景好漂亮！
example.en: Wow, the night view here is beautiful!

note: When something is unexpected or confusing.

example.zh: 咦？我的手機呢？
example.en: Huh? Where's my phone?

note: Sighing interjection.

example.zh: 唉，又要加班了。
example.en: Sigh, overtime again.

note: Tâi-lô pháinn-sè. Everyone, including non-Hokkien speakers, says it in its Taiwanese pronunciation ('pai-se'), never as Mandarin dǎi shì. Lighter than 對不起.

example.zh: 歹勢歹勢，我遲到了。
example.en: Sorry, sorry, I'm late.

note: Same word as 歹勢 (pháinn-sè), written with Mandarin characters that sound like it. Common in texts. Pronounced 'pai-se'.

example.zh: 拍謝，剛剛在忙沒看到訊息。
example.en: Sorry, I was busy and didn't see your message.

note: Tâi-lô a-má. The usual word for grandmother in Taiwan, even in Mandarin conversation (mainland 奶奶 / 外婆). Pronounced close to 'a-má'.

example.zh: 我阿嬤做的菜最好吃。
example.en: My grandma's cooking is the best.

note: Tâi-lô a-kong. The usual word for grandfather in Taiwan (mainland 爷爷 / 外公). Said like 'a-kong'.

example.zh: 阿公每天早上去公園運動。
example.en: Grandpa exercises in the park every morning.

note: Tâi-lô kóo-ì. Praise for an unpretentious, decent person. Usually said in Taiwanese: 'kóo-ì'.

example.zh: 他人很古意，不會騙你的。
example.en: He's an honest guy, he won't cheat you.

note: Tâi-lô tòng-suán (= 當選). Crowds chant 凍蒜！凍蒜！ at election rallies, always in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 選舉晚會大家一直喊凍蒜。
example.en: At the election rally everyone kept chanting 'elected!'

note: From Hokkien lia̍h-kông. Fully absorbed into Mandarin and said in Mandarin (zhuā kuáng); now also used on the mainland.

example.zh: 電腦當掉檔案全沒了，我快抓狂了。
example.en: My computer crashed and I lost all my files, I'm about to flip out.

note: Tâi-lô sio̍k koh tuā-uánn. Praise for cheap, generous food. Usually said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 這家自助餐俗擱大碗，學生最愛。
example.en: This cafeteria is cheap and generous, students love it.

note: Tâi-lô hó-khang. 好康報你知 = 'let me tell you about a great deal'. Often said in Mandarin as hǎo kāng.

example.zh: 有什麼好康的記得跟我說。
example.en: If there's a good deal, remember to tell me.

en: to blame others, drag others in
note: Tâi-lô khan-thua. Shifting blame unreasonably: 不要牽拖別人.

example.zh: 自己遲到還牽拖塞車。
example.en: He was late himself and blamed it on traffic.

note: Tâi-lô suí (properly written 媠). Written 水 because it sounds similar; said 'suí': 水喔！ = gorgeous!

example.zh: 哇，你今天好水喔！
example.en: Wow, you look gorgeous today!

note: Tâi-lô pha-pha-tsáu. Common in travel-show titles. Said either in Mandarin or Taiwanese.

example.zh: 放假就騎機車到處趴趴走。
example.en: On days off I ride my scooter all over the place.

en: savoury steamed rice cake in a bowl
note: Tâi-lô uánn-kué. A Tainan classic. Almost always ordered in Taiwanese: 'uánn-kué'.

example.zh: 台南的碗粿一定要吃看看。
example.en: You have to try Tainan's bowl rice cake.

note: Tâi-lô tsia̍h-pá--buē (食飽未). A traditional greeting, especially with older people; always said in Taiwanese. Mandarin equivalent: 吃飽了沒？

example.zh: 阿伯，呷飽沒？
example.en: Uncle, have you eaten yet?

note: Tâi-lô m̄-thang (毋通). Written with Mandarin sound-alike characters online; said 'm̄-thang'. 這樣母湯喔 = that's not OK.

example.zh: 上班時間睡覺，母湯喔！
example.en: Sleeping during work hours? Not OK!

note: From Taiwanese agreement 'heh--ah' (= 是啊). Extremely common in casual speech, even among Mandarin-dominant speakers.

example.zh: 「你也住板橋喔？」「嘿啊。」
example.en: 'You live in Banqiao too?' 'Yeah.'

note: Tâi-lô kóo-tsui. For babies, pets, cute behaviour. Said in Taiwanese ('kóo-tsui').

example.zh: 你家的狗好古錐喔！
example.en: Your dog is so cute!

note: Tâi-lô sam-pat. Teasing among friends (你很三八耶), but can be insulting, especially said of women. Said in Mandarin or Taiwanese.

example.zh: 你很三八耶，不要再鬧了。
example.en: You're so silly, stop messing around.

note: Calque of Hokkien ū-kàu. 有夠熱 = so hot; 有夠扯 = so ridiculous. Said in Mandarin (yǒu gòu).

example.zh: 今天有夠熱，根本不想出門。
example.en: It's so hot today, I don't want to go out at all.

en: can't stand it, can't take it
note: Tâi-lô tòng-bē-tiâu (擋袂牢). Used humorously in Mandarin conversation, said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 這麼辣我真的凍未條。
example.en: This spicy, I really can't take it.

note: From Hokkien àu-kheh ('rotten customer'). Said in Mandarin (ào kè); 奧 = bad, as in 很奧.

example.zh: 服務業最怕遇到奧客。
example.en: Service workers dread difficult customers.

note: Tâi-lô kòo-lâng-uàn. Usually said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 他講話很顧人怨，大家都不想理他。
example.en: The way he talks is obnoxious, nobody wants to deal with him.

note: Tâi-lô oo-pe̍h-kóng ('black-white talk'). Said in Taiwanese; Mandarin equivalent 亂講.

example.zh: 你不要黑白講，我沒有說過那種話。
example.en: Don't talk nonsense, I never said that.

note: Tâi-lô ké-pai. For people putting on airs. Said 'ké-pai'; can be fairly rude.

example.zh: 他講話很假掰，每句都夾英文。
example.en: He talks so pretentiously, English in every sentence.

note: Tâi-lô bah-uân. A translucent starchy dumpling with pork inside. Many people say 'bah-uân' even in Mandarin.

example.zh: 彰化的肉圓很有名。
example.en: Changhua's bah-uân are famous.

note: Tâi-lô oo-lián, from Japanese oden. Night-market and 7-Eleven snack; people say hēi lún in Mandarin or 'oo-lián'.

example.zh: 冬天晚上來一碗黑輪最舒服。
example.en: A bowl of oden on a winter night is the best.

note: Tâi-lô thian-puh-lah, from Japanese tempura via Hokkien. Usually said in Mandarin as tián bú là.

example.zh: 鹹酥雞我要加一份甜不辣。
example.en: Add an order of fish cake to my fried chicken.

note: Tâi-lô kóo-tsá-bī. Used in Mandarin (gǔ zǎo wèi) in ads and menus: 古早味紅茶, 古早味蛋糕.

example.zh: 這家紅茶是古早味的，很香。
example.en: This black tea is old-style, really fragrant.

note: Tâi-lô ūn-tsiàng, from Japanese untenshu via Hokkien. Usually said in Mandarin as yùn jiàng.

example.zh: 運將大哥很熱心，一路跟我聊天。
example.en: The taxi driver was really friendly, chatting with me the whole way.

note: Tâi-lô oo-bá-sáng, from Japanese obasan via Hokkien. Saying it to a woman's face is rude; 阿姨 is the polite address.

example.zh: 市場的歐巴桑都很會殺價。
example.en: The aunties at the market are great at haggling.

note: Tâi-lô oo-jí-sáng, from Japanese ojisan. As with 歐巴桑, not a polite form of address; use 先生 or 大哥.

example.zh: 那個歐吉桑每天都在公園下棋。
example.en: That old guy plays chess in the park every day.

note: Tâi-lô a-peh. Friendly way to address an older man in daily life.

example.zh: 阿伯，請問這附近有郵局嗎？
example.en: Uncle, is there a post office near here?

note: Tâi-lô thâu-ke. The owner's wife is 頭家娘. Usually said in Taiwanese; Mandarin 老闆.

example.zh: 頭家，這個怎麼賣？
example.en: Boss, how much is this?

note: Tâi-lô thâu-khak pháinn--khì ('head broken'). Said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 這麼熱還穿外套，你頭殼壞去喔？
example.en: Wearing a jacket in this heat, are you out of your mind?

note: Tâi-lô phiat-pōo. Very common in Mandarin conversation and headlines: 省錢撇步 = money-saving tips. Said as piě bù or 'phiat-pōo'.

example.zh: 你有沒有什麼讀書的撇步？
example.en: Do you have any study tricks?

note: Tâi-lô hó-ka-tsài. Relief after a close call; usually said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 好家在有趕上最後一班捷運。
example.en: Phew, I caught the last MRT.

note: Tâi-lô tshài-tshī-á-miâ ('market name' — call it in a market and many people turn around). Said in Taiwanese.

example.zh: 怡君是菜市仔名，我們班就有三個。
example.en: Yi-jun is a really common name, there were three in my class.

note: Tâi-lô mài (莫). Mostly in set phrases and texts: 麥擱來 (don't come again), 麥鬧了 (stop messing around).

example.zh: 好了，麥鬧了。
example.en: OK, quit messing around.

note: Tâi-lô lāu-khuì. Said in Taiwanese; 很漏氣 = so lame/embarrassing.

example.zh: 第一次約會就遲到，真漏氣。
example.en: Late for a first date, how embarrassing.

note: Tâi-lô lāu-pháu. Fully used in Mandarin (luò pǎo): 老闆落跑了 = the boss skipped town.

example.zh: 說好要來幫忙，結果他落跑了。
example.en: He promised to help, then bailed.

note: Tâi-lô khí-siáu (起痟). 你起肖喔？ = are you nuts?

example.zh: 他突然起肖，把東西都丟了。
example.en: He suddenly lost it and threw everything away.

en: unreasonable, impossible to talk sense into
note: From Hokkien huan. Said in Mandarin (很番) for someone who won't listen to reason.

example.zh: 他很番，怎麼講都講不聽。
example.en: He's so unreasonable, he won't listen no matter what.

note: Tâi-lô siánn-mih. Used jokingly in Mandarin conversation and texts: 啥米？！

example.zh: 啥米？明天要考試？
example.en: What?! There's a test tomorrow?

note: Tâi-lô khan-tshiú. In Taiwanese 'my 牽手' means my wife (or husband). In Mandarin 牽手 is also simply 'hold hands'.

example.zh: 這是我的牽手，我們結婚三十年了。
example.en: This is my wife, we've been married thirty years.

note: Hokkien sue. Fully used in Mandarin: 很衰, 衰事, 衰神 (jinx).

example.zh: 今天很衰，出門就被雨淋。
example.en: Today's been so unlucky, I got rained on the moment I went out.

note: Tâi-lô ke-pô. 你很雞婆耶 = mind your own business (or, warmly, you didn't have to do that).

example.zh: 我只是雞婆提醒一下，你不要介意。
example.en: I'm just being nosy and reminding you, don't mind me.

note: From Hokkien kha (role). 小咖 = small fry. Said in Mandarin (dà kā).

example.zh: 這次活動請到很多大咖。
example.en: This event got a lot of big names.

note: Tâi-lô bô-lōo-īng. Usually said in Taiwanese; can be harsh.

example.zh: 這把傘沒路用，一吹就壞了。
example.en: This umbrella is useless, it broke at the first gust.

note: Tâi-lô thôo-tāu. In Taiwan 土豆 means peanuts (Mandarin 花生), NOT potatoes as on the mainland. 土豆麵筋 is a canned breakfast side.

example.zh: 刨冰上面要加土豆粉。
example.en: Put peanut powder on the shaved ice.

en: I did eat / I've eaten (有 + verb)
note: Taiwan uses 有 + verb to affirm that an action happened, mirroring the negative 沒有 + verb (from Hokkien ū). Standard mainland Mandarin would say 我吃了. Very common in Taiwan speech.

example.zh: 「你有吃早餐嗎？」「有，我有吃。」
example.en: 'Did you eat breakfast?' 'Yes, I did.'

note: 有沒有 + verb asks whether something happened: 你有沒有看到我的手機？ Answer with 有 or 沒有. Mainland speakers more often use 看到…了嗎？

example.zh: 你有沒有看到我的手機？
example.en: Did you see my phone?

note: 有在 + verb asks about or affirms a habit or ongoing activity: 你有在運動嗎？ (do you work out?), 我有在追這部劇.

example.zh: 你平常有在運動嗎？
example.en: Do you exercise regularly?

en: is it cold? / are you cold? (會 + adjective)
note: Taiwan uses 會 + adjective to ask about or describe a state: 會冷嗎？ 會不會太貴？ 不會辣 (it's not spicy). Mainland speakers more often say 冷不冷 / 冷吗.

example.zh: 冷氣這樣會冷嗎？要不要調高一點？
example.en: Is the AC too cold like this? Should I turn it up a bit?

note: 會不會 + adjective checks gently: 會不會太遠？ Also guessing: 他會不會忘了？ (could he have forgotten?).

example.zh: 走路過去會不會太遠？
example.en: Would it be too far to walk?

en: it's done / I've sorted it (用 = do, handle)
note: In Taiwan 用 often works as a general 'do, deal with, fix' verb, like mainland 弄: 我來用, 用好了嗎？, 東西用一用.

example.zh: 電腦我幫你用好了，你試試看。
example.en: I've sorted out your computer, give it a try.

en: let me show you (給 + person + verb)
note: 給 + person + verb means 'let someone do' or 'do for someone': 給你看, 給我想一下 (let me think), 給他用.

example.zh: 我拍了好多照片，給你看！
example.en: I took loads of photos, let me show you!

note: Taiwan marks ongoing actions with plain 在 + verb. 正在…呢 and V著呢 sound mainland or bookish.

example.zh: 我在吃飯，等一下再打給你。
example.en: I'm eating, I'll call you back later.

note: The standard casual invitation: 要不要一起去？ Answer 好啊 or 不用了.

example.zh: 我們要去看電影，你要不要一起來？
example.en: We're going to see a movie, want to come along?

note: At the end of a suggestion it softens: 我們先吃飯好不好？ Said with emphasis it's exasperated: 我很忙好不好！ (I'm busy, OK?!).

example.zh: 我們先吃飯，再討論好不好？
example.en: Let's eat first and discuss after, OK?

en: I'll head off first (先 = for now, ahead of others)
note: 先 before the verb softens leaving or postponing: 我先走了, 先這樣, 你先忙 (I'll let you get on with it). Sentence-final 先 (我走先) is Cantonese-style, not normal Taiwan usage.

example.zh: 你先忙，我先走了。
example.en: I'll let you get on with it, I'm heading off.

note: In Taiwan 等一下 is used as a time word meaning 'in a bit, later' (mainland 一会儿 / 待会儿): 我等一下打給你. It still also means 'wait a moment'.

example.zh: 我現在在開會，等一下回你。
example.en: I'm in a meeting now, I'll reply in a bit.

en: take a quick look (一下 softener)
note: Adding 一下 makes requests lighter: 等一下, 幫我看一下, 問一下. Taiwanese use it constantly where the mainland might use 一下儿 or VV.

example.zh: 可以幫我看一下這份資料嗎？
example.en: Could you take a quick look at this?

note: Affirmative-negative questions; with two-syllable words Taiwan often repeats only the first syllable: 好不好吃, 喜不喜歡, 可不可以.

example.zh: 這家牛肉麵好不好吃？
example.en: Is this beef noodle place any good?

note: 很 + noun describes something as typical of it: 很台, 很日本, 很文青 (hipster), 很男人.

example.zh: 這家店的裝潢很日本。
example.en: This shop's decor is very Japanese.

note: In Taiwan 還好 often means 'not that much': 會辣嗎？還好 (not very). Saying a meal was 還好 is lukewarm, not praise.

example.zh: 「會很辣嗎？」「還好，你應該可以吃。」
example.en: 'Is it very spicy?' 'Not really, you should be fine.'

note: Common praise: 不錯喔！ = nice one! 還不錯 = quite decent.

example.zh: 你的中文不錯喔！
example.en: Your Chinese is pretty good!

note: Taiwan likes V看看 / VV看 for 'try doing': 吃吃看, 問看看, 穿看看. Mainland would often say 尝尝 / 试试.

example.zh: 這個很好吃，你吃吃看。
example.en: This is really good, try some.

note: 他很會唱歌 = he's a great singer; 很會講 = smooth talker; 很會吃 = big eater.

example.zh: 她很會做菜，每道都好吃。
example.en: She's a great cook, every dish is delicious.

note: 好 as 'so, how' in exclamations is everywhere in Taiwan: 好累, 好熱喔, 好好吃.

example.zh: 這隻貓好可愛喔！
example.en: This cat is so cute!

note: 蠻 (often written 滿, mǎn) = quite, pretty. Very common in Taiwan: 蠻好的, 蠻貴的.

example.zh: 這家便當蠻好吃的，而且不貴。
example.en: This bento is pretty good, and it's cheap.

en: laughed until my stomach hurt (V到 + result)
note: Taiwan often uses 到 instead of 得 for extent: 累到不行, 熱到受不了, 好吃到哭.

example.zh: 那部電影好好笑，我笑到肚子痛。
example.en: That film was so funny I laughed till my stomach hurt.

note: 想說 introduces what you were thinking, often a reason or a mistaken assumption. Not 'I want to say'.

example.zh: 我想說你很忙，就沒打給你。
example.en: I figured you were busy, so I didn't call.

note: Taiwan prefers 剛剛 to 剛才.

example.zh: 你剛剛說什麼？
example.en: What did you just say?

note: Taiwan Mandarin basically doesn't use the 儿 suffix: 哪裡 (not 哪兒), 這裡, 一點, 好玩, 一會. 裡 is often pronounced nǎ li in fast speech.

example.zh: 你住在哪裡？
example.en: Where do you live?

note: Taiwanese reduplicate to soften: 一點點, 一下下, 有一點點貴.

example.zh: 我只會說一點點台語。
example.en: I only speak a little Taiwanese.

note: Softer, cuter 一下: 等我一下下.

example.zh: 等我一下下，我馬上好。
example.en: Give me a sec, I'm almost ready.

note: Taiwan uses 可以 for ability, permission and possibility where the mainland often uses 能: 你可以幫我嗎？ 可以刷卡嗎？

example.zh: 你明天可以早一點來嗎？
example.en: Can you come a bit earlier tomorrow?

note: Taiwan uses 台 for vehicles and machines: 一台車, 一台電腦, 一台冷氣. Mainland uses 辆 for vehicles.

example.zh: 我想買一台新的機車。
example.en: I want to buy a new scooter.

note: Taiwan uses 間 for shops, restaurants, companies, schools and rooms: 一間餐廳, 一間公司. Mainland usually uses 家 / 所.

example.zh: 這附近有一間很好吃的拉麵店。
example.en: There's a really good ramen place near here.

note: Taiwan uses 支 for phones, pens, videos and umbrellas: 一支手機, 一支筆, 一支影片. Mainland often uses 部 / 个 for phones.

example.zh: 我上個月換了一支新手機。
example.en: I got a new phone last month.

note: Taiwan uses 顆 for small round things where the mainland says 个: 一顆蛋, 一顆蘋果, 一顆球, 一顆心.

example.zh: 滷肉飯加一顆滷蛋。
example.en: Braised pork rice with a braised egg.

note: Taiwan uses 跟 for 'and, with' in speech: 我跟你, 跟他說. When 和 is used as 'and', many Taiwanese read it hàn.

example.zh: 我跟你一起去。
example.en: I'll go with you.

en: no way! not at all (rhetorical denial)
note: Denies a claim or deflects a compliment: 哪有！ 我哪有這樣說？

example.zh: 「你又遲到了。」「哪有！我才晚兩分鐘。」
example.en: 'You're late again.' 'No way! I'm only two minutes late.'

note: V了沒 asks if something has happened yet, influenced by Hokkien: 吃飽了沒？ 到了沒？ 好了沒？

example.zh: 你到了沒？我已經在門口了。
example.en: Are you here yet? I'm already at the entrance.

en: let's eat first and worry later
note: 先 + V + 再說 = do this first and deal with the rest later; 再說吧 alone = 'we'll see'.

example.zh: 不要想那麼多，先吃再說。
example.en: Don't overthink it, let's eat first.
